relation_quote: A single distributed body the size of a small barn, packed to its own brim because it *is* its own brim.

note: main_kind: place_mind or process, since the text first says what lives there is the act of becoming, then treats it as a being whose body is the grove.

relation_quote: A cold, patient, many-bodied resident that treats water tables like lungs, reedbeds like pistons, fungus like memory, and storms like meals—an organism as old in posture as the worn mountains beneath it, and as restless as the hiss of static running stem to stem at night.
note: relation: is or in (a single distributed animal whose body is the mire's peat, reeds and pools, but it is called a resident and never plainly the place); main_kind: place_mind or animals.

relation_quote: What lives here is the *system*, the whole thing as a running process, the bog and the trees and the moss and the mycelium and the frogs and the beetles and the birds and the people and the water and the particular quality of the light that comes through this canopy to reach this moss — all of it together, all of it in relation, all of it running on the ancient energy of rain falling on high ground and finding its way down, of sunlight being caught by chlorophyll and converted to structure, of structure falling apart and being rebuilt and falling apart again in cycles so long they look like stability.
note: main_kind: place_mind (the text's closing answer is the whole system) or animals (most of the length is a species-by-species account).

relation_quote: They ride on the backs of Latchlings when they need to travel quickly, and they sleep in the folds of the kelp-analogs, waking only when the pocket asks a question—something hummed low and warm, audible only as a change in the lullaby of industry.
note: relation: alive or in, the pocket has a pulse, breathes and asks questions across several sentences, but this may be only figurative.
